items.title: Stony Brook study finds viral BookTok bestseller Daggermouth is 60% AI-written
items.excerpt: Using the AI-detection tool Pangram, Stony Brook University researchers found that roughly one in five randomly sampled Kindle ebooks contain substantial AI-generated text - and flagged #BookTok favorite Daggermouth by H.M. Wolfe as 60% AI-written. A concrete, method-driven look at how AI-generated fiction is slipping into bestseller lists and how detection now works.

items.title: Judge gives final approval to the $1.5 billion Anthropic author-copyright settlement
items.excerpt: A federal judge approved the landmark $1.5 billion settlement over Anthropic's use of roughly 500,000 pirated books to train its Claude models, with authors and publishers eligible for about $3,000 per infringed work. The largest reported copyright recovery to date, it sets a reference point for how AI training on books gets licensed and paid for.

items.title: Bloomsbury set to collect ~$18.7m from the Anthropic AI-copyright settlement
items.excerpt: Bloomsbury became the first major publisher to quantify its share of the Anthropic settlement - about $18.7m across roughly 14,000 titles, generally split with authors. An early signal of how the AI-training copyright reckoning is beginning to translate into real payouts for publishers and writers.

items.title: Publishing Perspectives launches a course to help publishers navigate the AI age responsibly
items.excerpt: A four-week online course beginning January 2027 aims to give publishing professionals practical frameworks for implementing AI in editorial and production workflows and setting organizational policy. A signal of houses trying to operationalize AI in the craft rather than just debate it.

items.title: Around the Book World: Dutch publishers launch Bookpact.ai as AI-licensing control tightens
items.excerpt: This roundup gathers the week's AI-in-publishing moves: a Dutch publisher coalition's Bookpact.ai platform lets houses license books to AI firms title-by-title with set compensation, alongside the Bloomsbury/Anthropic payout and reports of AI firms buying secondhand German books for training. A snapshot of publishers building opt-in machinery for how their books feed AI.
